text:
Alex: Heads up — after pushing BMC fw 2.3.1 to eu-west-rack-5, ~6/24 p4 nodes failed to boot. IPMI UID LED is amber on several, OOB console times out. I think CMOS got reset and boot order + secure boot bit flipped. Anyone seen this with 2.3.1?
Priya: On it. Which exact hostnames?
Alex: p4-euw-03, p4-euw-05, p4-euw-07, p4-euw-12 — models p4d-48g-2 / p4d-48g-1. Inventory tags all p4-euw-*.
Sam: Can you paste the ipmitool output from one of them? run: `ipmitool -H <bmc> -U admin -P **** sel list` and `ipmitool -H <bmc> -U admin -P **** chassis bootparam get 5`
Alex: pasting quick snippet from p4-euw-05 console (redacted BMC host):
```
ipmi> sel list
1 | 03/18/2026 | System Event | Critical | System boot
...
Boot Parameter 5 (Boot Flag) : 0x06
Boot Info Valid               : yes
Boot Flags                    : Force PXE  (0x0002)
```
Priya: Boot flag shows Force PXE. That explains it. Any logs saying Secure Boot state?
Alex: console log shows `Secure Boot: disabled` after reboot.
Jon: If CMOS reset occurred the boot order will often revert to PXE. Quick remediation: set persistent boot to disk then power-cycle: `ipmitool -H <bmc> chassis bootdev disk persistent` then `ipmitool -H <bmc> power cycle`.
Priya: Tried that on p4-euw-05 but it still PXEed. The firmware also seems to clear the secureboot variable on next reboot. vendor syslog shows `EFIVAR: cleared SecureBoot`.
Marta: That matches a vendor regression we saw internally last quarter — certain BMC fw builds toggle an NVRAM reset flag. Did we enable nvram-reset-on-update in the FW config?
Alex: I didn't touch that flag during rollout; image had default from vendor. We rolled out without a staging smoke that checks efivars.
Sam: Two parallel actions: 1) rollback BMC on affected nodes (if quick) 2) vendor workaround: force reapply secure keys and set boot policy persistently via vendor tool. Example: `vendor-fwctl --host <bmc> set-efivar SecureBoot=1 && vendor-fwctl set-boot-policy --persist disk`
Priya: Rolling back 2 nodes now (p4-euw-03, p4-euw-05) — update: rollback on 2 succeeded, nodes booted normally. Rolling back rest will take ~45m.
ops-oncall: Escalating to oncall and opening INC-20260318-4. Please add node list and raw ipmitool output to the incident. Tagging security for secureboot implications.
Alex: Noting impact: Dedicated GPU pool capacity down ~25%, provisioning queue delayed, cost spike on fallback cloud instances.
Sam: Add a short-term guard: stop further 2.3.1 pushes to EU region and add a canary group of 2 nodes to any future BMC rollouts. Also add a runbook step that verifies `efivar -l` after fw update.
Marta: Vendor triaged — they reproduced the nvram-clear condition in their lab with 2.3.1. Patch incoming but flagged as behavioral regression.
Priya: I'll run a fleet job after rollback to set bootdev/disk persistent and reapply vendor keys on all p4-euw nodes. Job command: `parallel-ssh -i -h hosts.txt "vendor-fwctl set-boot-policy --persist disk && vendor-fwctl reapply-keys"`
Jon: Also update the release checklist: "verify secureboot persistence and boot order" as a required smoke test. Marking 2.3.2 as patch release.
Alex: Thanks all. I'll update the incident. Leaving a note to add a staging test that applies BMC fw + reboot and checks EFIVARS before rolling to prod.
deploy-bot: rollback job completed on 4/6 nodes (p4-euw-03,05,07,12). Remaining 2 being worked — see CI: https://ci.internal/reports/INC-20260318-4
Priya: Great — once remaining are done I'll kick the reapply-keys job. :thumbsup:
Alex: Awesome. Follow-up actions assigned in the incident. :eyes:
